title: TDDR Rising Narratives — Black Friday evening, Nov 27
summary: A snapshot of opposition narratives from the Right and the Far Left as of 5:30 PM ET Friday, Nov 27, 2026 (Black Friday). Built for TDDR (Too Dumb Didn't Read). Three new Right narratives rose during the day. N.J. Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy's 1990s ties to an al-Qaeda-linked charity and the 'Blind Sheikh,' plus a weekend speech to American Muslims for Palestine, drew 1,291 posts in 24 hours (24.75× its prior average; 1,012 in Friday's daytime hours versus 64 on Thursday). Reporting has not tied him to the charity's al-Qaeda activity (The Daily Princetonian). Trump's 'we got Greenland' line matched 2,750 posts (1.84×); Danish officials called it inaccurate, and the deal he signed affirms Danish sovereignty (Newsweek). A DeSantis remark that 'the KKK was founded by Democrats' matched 1,519 (6.36×); PolitiFact and AP rate that claim False. Trump's Somali attack grew: after his '2%' post he said 'the big investigation has to be Minnesota' (2,774 posts, up from 1,989 this morning). The USAID Files query is still the largest (12,452, down from 17,635), and Trump's GDP 'fake numbers' claim cooled to 6,080, but its newness keeps it at the top of the momentum ranking. On the Far Left, the Fetterman–DSCC backlash kept rising (1,864, 2.95×), and the Van Hollen challenge held steady (6,357) as a YouGov poll showing Democrats prefer him 40% to 19% circulated before Tuesday's Dec. 1 vote. Three faded cards were dropped (Jeffries deportees, Mamdani hotline, Talarico). No political topic was on the U.S. trends list, which was Black Friday and football. Every count, quote and fact-check comes from sources and X queries pulled this evening or carried over from this morning and labeled. Nothing here is invented.

oppositionNote.body: Right = narratives the Right is pushing after the Democratic midterm wave. Far Left = pressure on Democratic leadership and the incoming majority from the party's left. The new Hamawy card is tagged Right because it uses an incoming Democrat's past to brand the new majority as soft on terrorism. The new KKK card recasts the party's history to flip racism charges. The new Greenland card is a false claim from the President; we tag it Right because it comes from the Republican administration and its supporters, even though on X it spreads mostly through corrections. The Somali card turns Minnesota's fraud cases into a call to remove a mostly citizen community. The GDP card casts the midterm result as the product of 'fake' data. The USAID card casts a past Democratic administration's programs as a censorship operation. The Abrego Garcia card uses his departure to brand the Democrats who defended him. The 'do not certify' and audit cards cast doubt on elections Democrats won. The Fetterman, Van Hollen and Medicare for All cards are pressure from the party's left on Democratic leaders. The tag is the primary opposition frame.

methodology: Last updated Friday, Nov 27, 2026, 5:30 PM ET. This is a research snapshot for TDDR, not a live API, and it will go stale. U.S. X trends were pulled at about 5:15 PM ET. This morning's snapshot (Nov 27, 7:17 AM ET) is kept in the archive and was not overwritten. All twelve of its narratives were re-counted with the same queries so momentum compares like with like. The new 24-hour window overlaps this morning's by 14 hours (5 PM Thursday to 7 AM Friday ET), so each card also reports its 7 AM–5 PM ET Friday daytime count against the same hours Thursday. Thursday was Thanksgiving, so a Black Friday 'rise' partly reflects a holiday baseline. Three cards were dropped because they faded: Jeffries deportees (421 posts in the last 24 hours, 0.96×; this morning 1,377; 57 in Friday's daytime hours versus 1,013 Thursday), Mamdani hotline (460, 0.12×; this morning 1,193; 181 versus 913) and Talarico 'Texas stolen' (331, 0.70×; this morning 542; 107 versus 318). Their fact-checks remain in this morning's snapshot. Three cards were added with new queries: Hamawy, Greenland and the KKK claim. Other candidates were counted and not carved out as cards: a broader 'rigged/stolen midterms' query (2,248 posts, 0.71×; noted on the 'do not certify' card); the progressive prison-abolition debate after a New York Times essay (514 posts, 0.30×); and Tennessee Rep.-elect Victoria Broderick calling Thanksgiving a 'colonial holiday' (63 posts, from a near-zero base).

For each narrative we ran one English-language X search with x.get_posts_counts_recent at hourly granularity over a 167-hour window from 6:00 PM ET Friday, Nov 20, through 5:00 PM ET Friday, Nov 27. The sum is the 'seven-day' total; the last 24 hours (5:00 PM ET Thursday through 5:00 PM ET Friday) are the 24-hour count; the last 10 hours give the daytime count, compared with hours 25–34 back (7 AM to 5 PM ET Thursday). Daily bars are those hourly counts summed by UTC day. We counted named news or fact-check outlets whose coverage we opened or retrieved and cite on the card. Official pages, transcripts, archives, aggregators, Substack-style analysis pages, X News summaries and X posts are cited as sources but not counted as outlets; this evening that includes AMP's convention page and the Mar-a-Lago press-pool transcript posted by The Last Refuge. This evening we researched the new Hamawy, Greenland and KKK cards and re-researched the Somali and Van Hollen cards with fresh post samples; the GDP, 'do not certify' and Medicare for All cards add a line or an X News summary only; the other cards carry this morning's research and outlet counts and say so. No card topic was on the U.S. trends list.

Score = 50% volume index + 30% acceleration index + 20% coverage index. Volume index is 100 × log10(1 + last-24h posts) / log10(1 + the highest last-24h count in this set). Acceleration index is 100 × min(last-24h / prior daily average, 3) / 3, so a triple-or-higher average scores 100. Prior daily average is (seven-day total − last 24h) / 6. Coverage index is 70 × min(outlets, 7) / 7, plus 30 if the topic was on the U.S. X trends list when we pulled it. The GDP, Hamawy and KKK queries had small baselines before this week, so their acceleration indexes are maxed out; a multiple like 24.75× means 'new,' not 'twenty-five times bigger.' The Somali query's prior average is inflated by an earlier spike, so its acceleration index is low even though it rose during the day. The volume ceiling this evening is 12,452 (the USAID query), down from 17,635 this morning, which raises every other card's volume index. Read the post counts alongside the scores.

Counts are query matches, not unique posts or unique users, and queries can overlap. The new Hamawy query is his surname alone, so it catches defenders and news relays. The Greenland query requires Greenland plus Trump, acquired or Denmark, so it catches Danish corrections, mockery and unrelated Greenland policy news. The KKK query requires Democrat(s) or DeSantis plus KKK or Klan, so it catches rebuttals and older history arguments. The other queries are unchanged from this morning and carry the same caveats: the GDP query catches news relays and rebuttals; the USAID query catches rebuttals; the Somali query catches Minnesota fraud-case coverage and fact-check replies; the Abrego Garcia query catches news relays and his defenders; the Fetterman query catches primary news; the 'do not certify' query catches rebuttals and other countries' elections; the Medicare for All query catches supporters, opponents and unrelated 'M4A' uses; the Van Hollen query catches syndicated news. Replies are included. Sentiment is a qualitative label from relevancy-sorted post samples and from quotes in news coverage, not a scientific poll. This evening we pulled fresh samples for the Hamawy, Greenland, KKK, Somali and Van Hollen queries; the other cards carry this morning's sentiment and say so. Daily bar charts use UTC days (a UTC day starts at 7:00 PM ET the previous evening). Bars marked * are partial windows. Hourly charts are labeled in ET.

disinfo.caveatBody: New this evening: 'Hamawy has overt ties to terrorists' leaves out context: his work with the Benevolence International Foundation was five weeks of medical volunteering in 1994, eight years before Treasury designated it an al-Qaeda financier, and reporting has not tied him to its al-Qaeda activity; he testified for the defense at the Blind Sheikh's 1995 trial and says he condemns his violence (The Daily Princetonian; New York Post). 'We got Greenland' is inaccurate: Danish officials told Newsweek that the September security agreement the U.S. signed states Greenland is part of the Kingdom of Denmark; it expands U.S. military access, not ownership. 'The KKK was founded by the Democratic Party' is rated False: historians say Confederate veterans founded it in Pulaski, Tenn.; many members were Southern Democrats, but the party did not create it (PolitiFact; AP). On the Somali claims, PolitiFact rated Trump's earlier '92% don't work' figure wrong (about 72% of Somali Minnesotans 16 and older are in the labor force), and IBTimes UK found no data supporting the '2%' figure. Carried over from earlier snapshots: 'Only 2% of our Somalian population… have a job… without receiving Government Assistance… The others should be thrown out' has no stated source, and most of the people it targets cannot be 'thrown out': roughly 95% of Somalis in Minnesota are U.S. citizens, most born here, per the state demographer. Somali Minnesotans' labor-force participation (about 72% of those 16 and older in 2024) is above the state's 68%. Benefit use is high (84% received cash aid, food stamps or Medicaid in 2019–2023), so at most about 16% received none — not 2% (New York Post). 'Fake' pre-election GDP: AP reported BEA revises GDP and jobs data on a pre-set schedule 'without regard to the political calendar'; BEA's release attributes the 0.9-point revision to updated software-price and retail data, against a published average advance-to-second revision of 0.5 point. 'GDI killed $200 million in conservative ad revenue' is misleading: GDI's figure is a global, annual estimate of ad money redirected across thousands of sites it rated high-risk (What the Fact). 'Fake economic numbers just prior to the Election' / a 'RECORD SETTING ERROR' is false as stated. BEA released the Q3 revision from 3.4% to 4.3% on its previously announced schedule, not 'three weeks late'; the 0.9-point change was the largest since 2020 but tied for 16th since 1990 and smaller than a 1.2-point revision in Trump's first term (CNBC). Axios reported the claim of a 'purposeful' error was made without evidence; BEA attributed the change to updated software-price and retail-sales data. 'USAID got platforms to defund and deplatform outlets': a review of the release found no USAID award to GDI and no sign its pilot ran (The Media Now). 'Gillibrand is stepping down from the DSCC' is not so: she has said she will seek another term, and the next Senate Democratic leader will name the chair after the Dec. 1 vote (The Hill; The Intercept argued she should be replaced). 'The DSCC endorsed Fetterman' is misleading: Gillibrand said the committee would back him in the general election if he wins the primary, and she did not endorse him in a primary (NBC News; Newsweek; The Philadelphia Inquirer). 'The USAID Files prove USAID got platforms to defund and deplatform outlets' goes beyond the documents: the most-cited item, a 2022 Global Disinformation Index concept note, is a proposal with no budget or award, and no public record shows USAID funded it (DC News Line); Newsweek said it is unclear which proposals were carried out. 'Abrego Garcia is an MS-13 gang member' is not supported; fact-checkers found the claim rested on a 2019 informant's account and his clothing, and that he had no criminal conviction (PolitiFact; USA Today; Snopes, 2025). '38 million invalid voters' is not a finding of illegal votes: the figure's own source, Unite4Freedom, describes the 38 million as 'registrations flagged for further investigation – not 38 million proven illegal registrations,' and we found no official finding that any state's result is in doubt (Democracy Docket; WOWT).

Overnight posts were mostly re-shares of Trump's 'RECORD SETTING ERROR' line and viral 'NOTHING BACK' recaps of his Thanksgiving post, plus news relays. The AP reported Trump called the pre-election figures 'fake' and demanded an investigation of the Commerce Department, and noted that GDP and jobs data are revised on a pre-set schedule 'without regard to the political calendar.' BEA's Nov. 25 release says real GDP was revised up 0.9 point to 4.3%, mainly from revised software-price data and Census retail data, partly offset by lower health-care services spending; BEA's revision table puts the average advance-to-second revision at 0.5 point.
talkingPoints: They put out fake economic numbers right before the election to sink Republicans — then quietly fixed them after.
A 'record setting error,' three weeks late: the midterm result was built on rigged data.
The deep state at the statistics agencies picked the winner; investigate now.
The real economy is booming — Democrats won on a lie about it.
narratives.amplifiers: Trump's own Truth Social posts; @GuntherEagleman and copy-paste accounts (@shadygrooove, @Texpatriot26, @wtcrescuer911); @ThePatriotOasis, @ConstitustionX, @JB_Slear. Relayed neutrally by market feeds (@FirstSquawk, @DeItaone per @ClosingPrints) and CNBC.
narratives.whyItWorks: It hands a beaten party a no-fault explanation for the midterm wave: the voters weren't wrong, the numbers were. The revision is real and unusually large, so the claim starts from a true fact, and few people know GDP is estimated three times on a fixed calendar. It came from the President on a holiday, wrapped in a viral, joke-like 'thank you' format that spread as entertainment. And it fits a familiar pattern after Trump's firing of the BLS commissioner last year, so the base already distrusts federal statistics.
narratives.audience: The Republican base looking for an explanation of the midterm losses; election-integrity audiences already sharing 'do not certify' and audit claims; and market-watchers, who saw the post relayed by financial feeds.
narratives.counter: Stick to the calendar. BEA publishes three estimates of each quarter about a month apart; the Nov. 25 second estimate came out on the date announced in advance (CNBC; Axios). The revision was large but not a record — tied for 16th since 1990, and smaller than the 1.2-point revision in 2020 during Trump's first term. The 'fake' pre-election number was already a strong 3.4% that beat forecasts, so it could not have been a plot to make the economy look bad. And BEA sits in a Commerce Department run by Trump's own secretary, Howard Lutnick (Axios).

factChecks.claim: The pre-election GDP figure was 'fake' and its revision should be investigated.
factChecks.detail: AP reported that BEA routinely revises GDP, jobs and other data on a pre-scheduled basis without regard to the political calendar. BEA's release attributes the 0.9-point upward revision mainly to revised software-price and retail-sales data; its published average advance-to-second revision is 0.5 point.

factChecks.claim: The Q3 GDP revision from 3.4% to 4.3% was a 'RECORD SETTING ERROR' issued 'three weeks late.'
factChecks.detail: CNBC said Trump 'falsely deemed' the revision a mistake: it was released on BEA's previously announced schedule, was tied for 16th-largest since 1990, and was smaller than the 1.2-point revision in Q2 2020.

factChecks.claim: Pre-election GDP numbers were deliberately understated — a 'massive, and purposeful, error.'
factChecks.detail: Axios reported Trump made the allegation 'without evidence'; revisions are routine as fuller data arrive, and BEA explained this one by updated software-price and retail-sales data.

narratives.title: NEW: 'An al-Qaeda-tied terrorist sympathizer is going to Congress' — the Right turns on N.J. Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy over 1990s ties and a weekend speech to American Muslims for Palestine
narratives.sentiment: Alarmed and accusatory on the Right ('overt ties and support of terrorists'), with a smaller set of defenders calling the attacks Islamophobic and posting point-by-point rebuttals
narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts since 7 AM ET Friday, the most-viewed was @TriciaOhio: 'It should alarm every American, regardless of political affiliation, that Adam Hamawy, who has overt ties and support of terrorists, will be a member of the US Congress come January' (13,066 views, 814 likes at sampling). Others: @LoomerUnleashed tied him to an NBC ad she said was pulled and called him 'a defense witness for the Blind Sheikh' (3,973 views); @daliaziada recirculated video of a victory-night 'Allahu Akbar' chant (3,640 views); @EllieCohanim: 'many Americans missed Al Qaeda tied Hamawy being elected' (1,345 views); @Therealrobx: 'National security threat' (1,724 views). Pushback was small in reach: @Cathy2NotToday replied to DeSantis with a rebuttal noting the 1994 work was five weeks of medical volunteering as a 24-year-old student and accused critics of Islamophobia. This is a read of that sample, not a poll.
narratives.summary: New this evening. The query matched 1,291 posts in the last 24 hours (5 PM ET Thursday to 5 PM ET Friday), 24.75 times a prior daily average of about 52. Most of it came on Black Friday: 1,012 posts from 7 AM to 5 PM ET Friday, versus 64 in the same hours Thursday; the busiest hour was 11 AM Friday (204 posts). The New York Post (Nov. 26) and the Washington Examiner reported that the incoming New Jersey Democrat is scheduled to speak twice this weekend at American Muslims for Palestine's convention near Chicago, a group sued by the family of Hamas victim David Boim and probed by House and Senate committees. The posts revive his record: in 1994, as a medical student, he spent five weeks volunteering in Bosnia with the Benevolence International Foundation, which Treasury designated in 2002 as an al-Qaeda financier; in the early 1990s he traveled with Omar Abdel-Rahman, the 'Blind Sheikh,' translated for him and testified as a defense witness at his 1995 trial. The Daily Princetonian reported that Hamawy has not been tied to any of BIF's al-Qaeda-linked activities; his spokesperson called the questions 'gross and bigoted' and said he 'condemns that man's violent rhetoric and actions.' An X News summary on Friday named Gov. Ron DeSantis and NYC Council Member Vickie Paladino among the critics. This had no card this morning; it is carved out because it rose more than twentyfold in Friday's daytime hours.
talkingPoints: A man who worked for an al-Qaeda front and testified for the Blind Sheikh will sit in Congress in January.
He's headlining a Hamas-linked group's convention the same weekend.
This is who Democrats sent to Washington in the midterms.
Keep him off the national security committees.
The NJ GOP let him win without a fight.
narratives.amplifiers: Conservative and pro-Israel accounts: @TriciaOhio, @LoomerUnleashed, @daliaziada, @EllieCohanim, @trishaposner, @EndTimeHeadline; the New York Post and Washington Examiner stories; per X News, Gov. Ron DeSantis and NYC Council Member Vickie Paladino. Defenders include reply accounts such as @Cathy2NotToday and supporters who call the scrutiny bigoted.
narratives.whyItWorks: It strings together real, checkable facts — a Treasury-designated charity, a convicted terrorist, a group facing a terrorism lawsuit — and lets the audience fill in the conclusion that Hamawy shares their aims. A fresh news peg (the convention is this weekend) keeps it moving, and it lets the Right recast the Democrats' midterm wave as 'who voters sent to Washington.'
narratives.audience: Pro-Israel conservatives and Jewish voters worried about antisemitism, national-security hawks, New Jersey Republicans, and Republicans looking for a face for the incoming Democratic majority.
narratives.counter: Don't deny the facts; give the context the posts leave out. The BIF work was five weeks of medical volunteering in 1994, eight years before Treasury's designation, and reporting has not tied Hamawy to BIF's al-Qaeda activity (The Daily Princetonian). Testifying as a witness is not support for a crime, and he has condemned Abdel-Rahman's violence. He is a former Army surgeon. Speaking at a convention is not the same as the lawsuit's allegations being proven. Then ask whether the same standard is applied to everyone in Congress.

factChecks.detail: Reporting confirms he volunteered with the Benevolence International Foundation in Bosnia for five weeks in 1994, eight years before Treasury designated it an al-Qaeda financier, and testified for the defense at Omar Abdel-Rahman's 1995 trial. The busiest hour was 2 PM Friday (159 posts). X News summaries on Friday said Gov. Ron DeSantis stated the Ku Klux Klan was founded by Democrats, not Republicans; conservatives amplified it with timelines and memes, and critics pointed to the 20th-century realignment of the parties. PolitiFact rated the claim that 'the KKK was formed by the Democratic Party' False: historians say a handful of Confederate veterans founded it in Pulaski, Tenn., as a social club that turned violent; many members were Southern Democrats and Klans acted as a 'strong arm' for local Democratic politicians, but there is no evidence the party founded it. talkingPoints: The KKK was founded by Democrats — that's history, not opinion.
Democrats were the party of slavery, segregation and Jim Crow.
Robert Byrd was a Klan recruiter and a Democratic senator.
Democrats are still oppressing Black Americans today.

narratives.amplifiers: Gov. Ron DeSantis (per X News); conservative reply accounts such as @KevinMi02072897, @AmFodalo7, @danc16f and @GaryVwaze; X News summaries. Pushback from progressive reply accounts (@Z_Archer25).
narratives.whyItWorks: It starts from a kernel of truth — many early Klansmen were Southern Democrats — and drops the century of realignment that followed, so it is hard to rebut in one reply. It flips a racism charge back on Democrats and gives a party in post-midterm retreat a history lesson to share instead of a policy fight.
narratives.audience: Conservative base voters, Republicans courting Black and Hispanic voters, and DeSantis supporters as he hints at a 2028 run.
narratives.counter: Concede the kernel, then finish the history: the Klan was started by six Confederate veterans, not by a party; PolitiFact rates 'the Democratic Party created the KKK' False. The parties' platforms flipped after the Civil Rights Act of 1964, when segregationist 'Dixiecrats' left the Democratic Party. Ask what any of it says about policy today.

narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts since 7 AM ET Friday, the most-viewed were The New Yorker's interview post (10,557 views at sampling), Face the Nation's Sunday booking (5,927), the Daily Signal calling both men 'ideological weathervanes competing over who can promise the most freebies' (2,373) and @ctelectionguide's report of the Connecticut chairs' letter (1,907). From 7 AM to 5 PM ET Friday (Black Friday) the query matched 3,464 posts, versus 3,445 in the same hours Thursday (Thanksgiving). Holding in daytime hours. Friday's push: Common Dreams highlighted an Economist/YouGov poll (Nov. 20–23) in which Democratic voters preferred Van Hollen over Schumer 40% to 19%, with a call to 'call your senators now'; 70 Connecticut Democratic town committee chairs urged Sens. Chris Murphy and Richard Blumenthal to back Van Hollen (@ctelectionguide); The New Yorker ran an interview in which Van Hollen called Schumer's leadership 'for way too long, a one-man band'; and CBS's Face the Nation booked him for Sunday. The secret-ballot caucus vote is Tuesday, Dec. 1 (this morning's top summary called it Monday; Dec. 1 is a Tuesday). X News said Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Ed Markey remain neutral. This morning's card (Nov. 27, 7:17 AM ET): 6,341 posts in the last 24 hours (7 AM ET Thursday to 7 AM ET Friday), 0.84 times the prior daily average of about 7,530 (last evening: 8,751 and 1.20×). From 5 PM ET Thursday (Thanksgiving) to 7 AM ET Friday the query matched 2,896 posts, versus 5,301 in the same hours a night earlier. Cooling overnight. The story in X News summaries late Thursday ET was a Schumer campaign aide's edit of the celebrity and donor letter backing Van Hollen. POLITICO reported that spokesman Angelo Roefaro, who had access to the letter's Google Doc, added Frank Sinatra (who died in 1998) as a signatory, briefly changed the endorsement to Schumer and sent mocking texts to the consultant who drafted it; he said 'Chuck has no idea about any of this. I did it My Way' (Mediaite; Just The News). Deadline reported the letter's roughly three dozen signers include Robert De Niro, Jane Fonda and Chelsea Handler. A separate query for the prank (Roefaro, or Schumer with Sinatra, 'celebrity letter,' De Niro or prank) matched 407 posts in the last 24 hours, 0.80× its prior average. Some Democrats called for Roefaro to be fired (Mediaite).

Ruffalo is right: leadership should follow the will of the people. (Critics: that line is the 'dual loyalty' smear.)

narratives.amplifiers: Far Left and progressive: @commons96055467 (409 likes), @joshforprogress, @matsoR ('both Senators from… Michigan back Chris Van Hollen'), plus Sens. Bernie Sanders and Jeff Merkley and Sens.-elect Abdul El-Sayed and Peggy Flanagan. Reporters and aggregators: @jsolomonReports, @JustTheNews, @CraigCaplan, @LauraEWeiss16, @TIME. On the other side, Schumer's backers include Sen. Angela Alsobrooks.
narratives.whyItWorks: Each new endorsement is a fresh, concrete news peg in a race with a date, a vote count (28) and a clear villain for the left: a 76-year-old leader who has led Democrats since 2017. Slotkin is a moderate, so her backing lets the left argue the challenge is mainstream, not fringe. The filibuster clip gives supporters a simple promise to share.
narratives.audience: Progressive and younger Democrats, Sanders and El-Sayed voters, activists who blame Schumer for past compromises, and political-insider audiences following the whip count.
narratives.counter: Treat it as a normal leadership race, not a crisis: the caucus votes by secret ballot on Dec. 1 and most senators have not declared (The Washington Post; The Hill). Keep the focus on the agenda both candidates say they want, lower costs and a faster Senate, and note that Van Hollen himself says rules changes are the caucus's call (Roll Call).

narratives.title: NEW: 'We got Greenland' — Trump says the U.S. acquired Greenland; Denmark says the security deal he signed affirms it is Danish
narratives.query: Greenland (Trump OR acquired OR Denmark) lang:en
narratives.sentiment: Mostly mockery and correction (Danish users: 'We didn't give you Greenland, Donald'); a smaller MAGA stream celebrates it as a win
narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts since 7 AM ET Friday, the most-viewed was a Danish user's reply: 'Dane here. We didn't give you Greenland, Donald. You signed a security deal' (@Gianl1974, 14,517 views, 714 likes at sampling). News relays led the rest: @GlobalNewsHQI's 'TRUMP SAYS: "WE GOT GREENLAND!"… But… America did NOT acquire the island' (2,229 views) and @AnnevanLeur's 'Denmark Hits Back at Trump' (513 views). Replies called the claim a lie and quoted Grok on the deal's terms. We saw few posts in this sample repeating the claim approvingly. This is a read of that sample, not a poll.
narratives.summary: New this evening. The query matched 2,750 posts in the last 24 hours (5 PM ET Thursday to 5 PM ET Friday), 1.84 times its prior daily average of about 1,496; 1,470 came from 7 AM to 5 PM ET Friday, versus 110 in the same hours Thursday. The busiest hour was 1 PM Friday (182 posts). After meeting NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte at Mar-a-Lago on Thursday evening, Trump told reporters that allies 'weren't very helpful to us on… Iran. But, we got Greenland, and we got Greenland. That's three times the size of Texas, and that made me feel a little bit differently' about U.S. troops in Europe (Newsweek). Danish officials told Newsweek on Friday the claim was 'inaccurate': 'Greenland is part of Denmark. Trump hasn't got Greenland,' and 'the Security Agreement that the US signed states that.' The Sept. 22 agreement, signed by Trump and the Danish and Greenlandic prime ministers, updates a 1951 defense pact: more U.S. activity at Pituffik Space Base and two new defense areas, while affirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination (Newsweek; Hindustan Times; Outlook India). Newsweek said Trump made a similar claim earlier this month on Fox News, when co-host Brian Kilmeade clarified he meant a military agreement. It is tagged Right because it is a false claim from the President; on X it is spreading mostly through corrections.
talkingPoints: We got Greenland — three times the size of Texas.
Trump did what no president could: Greenland is ours.
Europe didn't help on Iran, but Greenland changes the math on troops.
Critics mocked the Greenland push; now look who won.
narratives.amplifiers: Trump's own remarks to the press pool at Mar-a-Lago; MAGA accounts celebrating it. Corrections came from Danish officials via Newsweek, Danish and European users (@Gianl1974, @AnnevanLeur), news relays (@GlobalNewsHQI) and Grok replies.
narratives.whyItWorks: It turns a technical defense agreement into a simple real-estate win with a vivid size comparison, and it links to Trump's long-running Greenland push, so supporters hear a promise kept. Repetition (Fox earlier this month, Thursday again) makes the word 'got' stick even as officials correct it.
narratives.audience: Trump supporters who backed the Greenland push; America First voters skeptical of NATO. The corrections reach Europeans and Trump critics.
narratives.counter: Quote the deal: it expands U.S. military access (Pituffik, two new defense areas) and affirms the Kingdom of Denmark's sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination. factChecks.detail: The New York Post said Trump cited no source. It reported that about 72% of Somali Minnesotans 16 and older were in the labor force in 2024, that 84% of the Somali diaspora in Minnesota received cash aid, food stamps or Medicaid in 2019–2023 (so at most about 16% received none), and that roughly 95% are U.S. citizens, most born in the U.S.

narratives.title: '38 million invalid voters — do not certify' — still a top-three query, but its daytime count halves as copy-paste reply campaigns carry it
narratives.query: ("do not certify" OR "don't certify" OR "dont certify" OR "withhold certification" OR "stop the certification" OR "38 million invalid") lang:en
narratives.sentiment: Insistent but recycled: the same Joe Hoft headline pasted into replies; a fringe 'storm the Capitol' reply; more 'show us the 38 million' and 'Joe made up the number' pushback
narratives.sentimentNote: We did not pull a fresh post sample for this card this evening or this morning; the sentiment label is carried over from an earlier snapshot. Earlier note: In a relevancy sample of posts from 7 AM to 5 PM ET Wednesday, the most-engaged post was '38 million invalid voters! There is no way in heck this election can be certified' (@Jessies_Too, 1,852 views, 328 likes). Much of the rest was one account pasting the same 'SERIOUS QUESTIONS ABOUT WHETHER US ELECTION SHOULD EVEN BE CERTIFIED: 38 MILLION INVALID VOTERS' line into replies to other users (@PatrJoe, at least eight times in about six minutes). One reply urged, 'Storm the Capitol to stop the certification of the results!' (@BCGrp_LLC, 33 views). Pushback grew: 'There aren't 38 million invalid votes' (@Edward_Morling), 'Joe made up the 38 million invalid voter number' (@seikjaboote) and 'Show us the facts behind 38 million invalid voters' (@dukelu78). This is a read of that sample, not a poll.
narratives.summary: Evening update (Nov 27): 7,039 posts in the last 24 hours (5 PM ET Thursday to 5 PM ET Friday), 0.29 times the prior daily average of about 24,313 (this morning: 6,299 and 0.25×). From 7 AM to 5 PM ET Friday (Black Friday) the query matched 3,951 posts, versus 3,210 in the same hours Thursday (Thanksgiving). Rising in daytime hours. One of the few carried queries that rose in daytime hours. An X News summary on Friday ('Democrats Secure House and Senate in 2026 Midterms Amid Rigging Claims') said conservative posts alleged manipulation as results certify and that fact-checkers have debunked the voter-fraud narratives. A broader query for 'rigged,' 'stolen,' 'fraud' or 'manipulated' with 'midterm(s)' matched 2,248 posts (0.71×), with 1,770 in Friday's daytime hours versus 475 on Thursday. We did not re-research this card this evening; its sources and outlet count are carried over from this morning. This morning's card (Nov. 27, 7:17 AM ET): 6,299 posts in the last 24 hours (7 AM ET Thursday to 7 AM ET Friday), 0.25 times the prior daily average of about 25,000 (last evening: 10,134 and 0.41×). From 5 PM ET Thursday (Thanksgiving) to 7 AM ET Friday the query matched 3,089 posts, versus 6,923 in the same hours a night earlier. Cooling overnight.
talkingPoints: 38 million invalid voters means no honest certification is possible.
There's no chain of custody for mail-in ballots and the machines were built for fraud.
Governors and secretaries of state must not certify until every vote is verified.
Trump should declare an emergency and audit all 50 states.
Democrats stole America.
narratives.amplifiers: Right: Joe Hoft (joehoft.com) and Unite4Freedom's Harry Haury; @jjauthor (the most-engaged post in our sample); Kari Lake ('Do not certify until you VERIFY the vote,' earlier this month); activists such as Kevin Sorbo, Gunther Eagleman and Scott Presler, whom X News named in the related push against Senate Republicans; and many small accounts quote-posting Hoft.
narratives.whyItWorks: A huge round number sounds like an audit finding, and the article borrows the language of federal law (NVRA, HAVA) and accounting ('material' errors). It hands disappointed voters one concrete demand with a deadline — don't certify — as states finish their canvasses this month. It joins the Michigan Wi-Fi and forensic-audit claims into one story, and the size of the Democratic wave makes a stolen election feel plausible to people who never saw it coming.
narratives.audience: Trump voters stunned by the landslide; election-integrity activists; Republican county and state officials facing certification deadlines; low-trust voters who read messy voter rolls as proof of illegal votes.
narratives.counter: Use their own source. Unite4Freedom says the 38 million are records 'flagged for further investigation,' not proven illegal registrations, and a voter roll with people who moved or died is not a ballot cast illegally. Certification is a legal duty, not a vote of confidence, and Iowa's Republican secretary of state defended his state's results. Point out who isn't buying it: Cleta Mitchell, Michael Flynn and Stop the Steal's Ali Alexander all said this landslide was real (Democracy Docket).
